OTHER NOTES:

> 1.3.3 Verify that data being passed to a potentially dangerous context is sanitized
beforehand to enforce safety measures, such as only allowing characters
which are safe for this context and trimming input which is too long.


The statement is too general and doesn’t clearly define what to consider as a “potentially dangerous context” what “safe characters” are, or what qualifies as proper sanitization. Without more concrete details, the requirement is open to interpretation and could lead to insufficient or incorrect sanitization, leaving the application vulnerable.

comments.body: I agree this is (way) too general and propose we just remove it.
This is sort of designed as a catch all for circumstances we don't cover specifically, that is why it is here. I agree it isn't perfect but it is trying to set a baseline.

> This is sort of designed as a catch all for circumstances we don't cover specifically, that is why it is here. I agree it isn't perfect but it is trying to set a baseline.

I would suggest we move it to chapter text instead. It's too high level to be actionable.
This is the most important requirement for the section and has the catch-all goal, as Josh said. The requirement is a must-have and needed for a testing and reporting point of view.

> This is sort of designed as a catch all for circumstances we don't cover specifically, that is why it is here. I agree it isn't perfect but it is trying to set a baseline.

If this isn’t perfect and the goal is just to set a baseline, then why shouldn’t it be written as chapter text?
because it is a baseline requirement, I am going to close this issue for now.
